Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-09 16:00 PST
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Platform: Zoom (recording available)

Maya: quick alignment on co-sell motion, pricing tiers, and pilot logistics. Devon: technical constraints for Dedicated and VPC. Ravi & Elena: timeline for co-sell approvals and top accounts. Action items agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 50 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Ravi Shah: Hi this is Ravi — sorry for the slight delay, had back-to-back.
[00:09] Elena Morales: Elena here.
[00:10] Tom Nguyen: Tom, solutions.
[00:11] Sara Lim: Sara from finance, hi.
[00:13] Devon Patel: Devon, Redwood SE.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Lena, CSM at Redwood.
[00:17] Maya Chen: Awesome. Goal for today — align on opportunity orchestration: which accounts we push together, fine tune the co-sell pricing band, and make sure the pilot + security checklist is clear so procurement can move fast. Does that sound right?
[00:27] Ravi Shah: That's perfect. We also wanna, like, make sure the partner exec briefing is in place before we go to customers.
[00:31] Elena Morales: Yep, and one ask — we need a straightforward deal registration flow so our field folks can register and not — not get blocked by discount approvals.
[00:37] Maya Chen: Absolutely. For the pricing piece, we proposed a three-tier discount band in the one-pager: co-sell referral (5%), joint-sell (10%), and committed pipeline (15%) with a minimum ARR. Is that acceptable to you?
[00:50] Sara Lim: Uh, finance will need to see the net margins. 15% is— it's a little high unless there's a firm commit or marketing fund attached.
[00:57] Maya Chen: Totally understood. We can make 15% conditional on a 12-month commit and joint marketing investment — co-funded exec brief, webinar credits. Does that help?
[01:07] Ravi Shah: Yeah, that helps. For the top accounts — we prepared a list of 12 to start. We think 6 are high priority where Orion has exec relationships and the other 6 are motion plays.
[01:17] Devon Patel: Quick technical note on those high-priority accounts: a couple of them require data residency in eu-west-1 and one insists on customer-managed KMS. We need to confirm Private / Dedicated compliance on that.
[01:28] Tom Nguyen: For the KMS question — can Redwood support a bring-your-own-key for Dedicated? We saw references in the docs but wanted confirmation.
[01:35] Devon Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports BYOK via the KMS integration; for Private (VPC) we'll need a short runbook for the key rotation and HSM proof. We'll supply the outline.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Good. And on SOC 2 / compliance — we can share the security pack but Tom, can you put together the top 3 compliance questions your procurement will ask so we pre-empt them?
[01:54] Tom Nguyen: Yep, I'll do that. Probably around data retention, audit logs, and SSO/SAML integration.
[01:59] Elena Morales: For our sellers, the simplest thing is a one-pager that says "who owns the account, how to register, discount thresholds, and contact for escalations." Can Redwood draft that?
[02:09] Maya Chen: We'll draft it. Lena, can you own the one-pager and the co-sell SOP?
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: Yep, happy to.
[02:14] Maya Chen: Cool. Let's walk through the pilot scope — Devon, want to cover the technical plan?
[02:18] Devon Patel: Sure. We propose a 2-week smoke test on Redwood Dedicated with 3 models: a base-L, a quantized medium, and a low-cost embedding workflow. We'll measure p95 latency, throughput under sustained load, and token cost. Also validate KV cache behavior for chat sessions.
[02:32] Ravi Shah: How quickly can we spin that up?
[02:34] Devon Patel: If we get sample prompts and a dataset by Thursday, we can stand up Dedicated in our test pool within 48 hours and run the smoke test within the week. So technically by next Tuesday we could have initial numbers.
[02:45] Sara Lim: About pricing during pilot — will there be credits or discounted pilot rates?
[02:49] Maya Chen: Yes, we typically provide pilot credits and a temporary discounted pilot rate. We'll include that in the one-pager. For procurement, we'll draft a simple order form.
[02:57] Elena Morales: Good. Also want to confirm the process for joint customer outreach — do we have a suggested sequence? Raven — I mean, sorry — Maya?
[03:06] Maya Chen: (laughs) We'll do an intro email, then joint exec brief, then technical workshop, then pilot. For closed-won, we'll do joint case study and co-marketing. We should map owners per account in the next step.
[03:17] Ravi Shah: Perfect. On competitive dynamics — GoliathAI has been pitching one of our targets with heavy discounting. We need early exec engagement to neutralize that.
[03:26] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize that account for an executive call. Devon, any risks you see from a technical POV on that account?
[03:33] Devon Patel: One of their use cases is long-context chat with streaming. We should test token streaming under 8k sequences; our Dedicated profile handles that but we need to validate in their specific prompt shapes.
[03:44] Tom Nguyen: We'll send sample long-context transcripts. Also note: they require HIPAA considerations for a sub-vertical customer — are there addendums for BAAs?
[03:52] Maya Chen: Redwood has a BAA template for enterprise deals. I'll attach that.
[03:56] Lena Ortiz: I'll pull the legal checklist and the security pack.
[03:59] Ravi Shah: Great. I wanted to circle back to deal registration — Elena, what does your field need to trigger registration?
[04:05] Elena Morales: They need the account, anticipated ARR band, and a named AE at Redwood to assign. Also a short proof of joint motion plan. If that's in the one-pager they can file quickly.
[04:14] Maya Chen: We'll include a registration form link and a template.
[04:17] Sara Lim: Timeline wise — procurement is slower this quarter; our target close for the first two accounts is end of Q1 2027. We need the pilot in Nov/Dec to align with that.
[04:28] Maya Chen: That timeline makes sense. Let's set milestones: pilot by mid-November, exec briefing late Nov, procurement kickoff early December.
[04:36] Ravi Shah: Sounds good.
[04:38] Speaker 3: um hi this is — sorry, i just joined — quick question on revenue split, how are renewals counted?
[04:44] Maya Chen: Good question. Renewals count based on net revenue associated with Redwood contracts; commission or split details we'll map in the co-sell agreement. We'll propose a renewal credit structure in the doc.
[04:55] Devon Patel: Technical wrinkle — if we do on-prem (Private) for one customer, some monitoring hooks change. We'll need a quick ops runbook to show what telemetry is available.
[05:05] Tom Nguyen: Ops runbook is critical for our SRE teams. Can Redwood provide a sample runbook?
[05:09] Devon Patel: Yes, we have a Private deployment runbook and a Dedicated monitoring guide. I'll attach both.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Okay, shifting briefly to pricing mechanics — Sara, is your concern more about the headline discount or the net margin after services?
[05:23] Sara Lim: Net margin. We need to see the total TCO including integration costs. If Redwood can help with a low-friction onboarding credit for the first customer, that helps.
[05:33] Maya Chen: We can propose an onboarding/enablement credit for the first co-sell partner customer per account — maybe $15k or a % credit. We'll put options in the pricing sheet.
[05:43] Elena Morales: Also want to avoid too many manual approvals. If we can automate discounts based on ARR thresholds in the form, our field can self-serve.
[05:51] Maya Chen: We'll include an automated banded discount table and a simple approval escalation contact.
[05:56] Ravi Shah: For the pilot acceptance criteria — what are you thinking? Latency under X, accuracy within Y, and integration readiness?
[06:03] Devon Patel: Proposed acceptance: p95 latency < 350ms for the base-L for chat cases, embedding 99% availability during smoke run, and successful SSO auth and key rotation test. We'll draft metric thresholds and instrumentation.
[06:17] Tom Nguyen: On SSO — we use Okta; Redwood supports SAML and OIDC, correct?
[06:22] Devon Patel: Yes, both. We'll need a test Okta connector.
[06:26] Sara Lim: About contract terms — do we have minimums for Dedicated?
[06:30] Maya Chen: Dedicated reserved capacity has a minimum monthly commit — we can discuss flexible options for the pilot. For production, there is typically a 3–12 month committed capacity term depending on the tier. We'll lay out examples.
[06:40] Elena Morales: If we commit to a subset of accounts and hit ARR targets, can we get expanded co-marketing funds?
[06:45] Maya Chen: Yes, co-marketing and MDF can scale with committed pipeline milestones. We'll show a ladder.
[06:50] Ravi Shah: Okay, I have one operational ask: when the field registers a deal, can Redwood auto-provision a sandbox Dedicated instance for demos? That would help shorten cycles.
[06:59] Devon Patel: We have a sandbox flow, but auto-provisioning needs a registration trigger and a seat license. We can automate it for registered deals if we tie it to a short form. We'll coordinate with your ops.
[07:11] Maya Chen: Let's capture that as an action — Devon will prototype an automation flow for sandbox provisioning.
[07:16] Devon Patel: Noted.
[07:18] Maya Chen: Quick check — any blockers from legal/security before we share the full pack?
[07:22] Tom Nguyen: Nothing major. We do want the SOC and pen test summary up front.
[07:26] Lena Ortiz: We'll share SOC 2 and the latest penetration test summary.
[07:28] Ravi Shah: Great.
[07:30] Speaker 2: one tiny — sorry, is there an MSA or will we use our standard?
[07:34] Maya Chen: Redwood has a standard MSA and we can give the BAA and other addendums; we can also accommodate Orion's redlines in larger deals.
[07:42] Sara Lim: For procurement clarity — please include a sample SOW for the onboarding work.
[07:46] Maya Chen: Will do.
[07:47] Devon Patel: For the benchmark plan — can Orion send a set of 10 representative prompts and a sample corpus? Preferably anonymized.
[07:55] Tom Nguyen: We'll send that by Friday.
[07:57] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll summarize next steps — 1) Redwood to send co-sell one-pager + pricing options + legal/security pack (owner: Maya/Lena) — due 11/12. 2) Orion to share top-10 target accounts and sample prompts (owner: Ravi/Tom) — due 11/13. 3) Devon to run Dedicated smoke test and share metrics (owner: Devon) — due 11/17. 4) Schedule exec briefing for week of 11/23 (owner: Maya). Does that capture it?
[08:22] Ravi Shah: Yes.
[08:24] Elena Morales: Yes.
[08:25] Sara Lim: Yes.
[08:26] Maya Chen: Ok last quick thing — for the co-sell field enablement, can Redwood provide a 30–45 minute playbook webinar?
[08:32] Lena Ortiz: Yep, we can run that and record it for the field.
[08:35] Elena Morales: That would be perfect.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Great. Any other questions?
[08:39] Tom Nguyen: None from me.
[08:40] Ravi Shah: No.
[08:41] Sara Lim: No.
[08:42] Maya Chen: Awesome — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the attachments and meeting notes. Next meeting — let's tentatively set a pilot check-in for 2026-11-18.
[08:51] Elena Morales: Works for me.
[08:53] Maya Chen: Thanks all. Bye.
